analysis: No documented process for recording the basis on which a consumer's best interest was determined. Three of the five files sampled carried no rationale at all.
Policy refers to the previous terminology and has not been reissued. The underlying control operates, but the procedure supporting it is not written down.

Vulnerability material exists across training and guidance documents but there is no standalone policy, and records of identified circumstances are not available to staff providing ongoing assistance.
No evidence that trusted contact persons have been nominated, or that the written consents this provision requires have been obtained.
No policy or procedure for employees to raise a concern that a consumer is at risk of financial abuse.
Digitalisation requirements are met. The online journey was walked end to end and the required disclosures appear at each decision point.
Disclosures are present but two of them appear after the point of commitment rather than before it.
Charges are disclosed in the required form and the schedule is current.
Provision may not be engaged by this entity's permissions. Scope to be confirmed with the client before this is assessed.
Advertising approval log does not record who approved each item or on what date, so the control cannot be evidenced retrospectively.
Errors resolution procedure meets the requirement and the log is complete for the period.
Complaints are resolved within the required timeline but the final response letters do not consistently state the right of referral.
Records retention meets the required period and the retrieval test performed on 11 Jun 2026 succeeded.
Applies only to activities the entity may not carry on. Confirm permissions.
Standards for Business have not been mapped to existing policies, so it cannot be shown which internal document discharges each standard.
Board has approved the standards in principle. No evidence of the ongoing oversight the supporting standards require.
Governance arrangements meet the supporting standard.
